subject: [PATCH v5 0/3] x86/tdx: Fix port I/O handling bugs

reviews.author: Sean Christopherson
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Sean Christopherson argued that using a mask for the 4-byte port I/O case would defeat consistency in handling different port sizes, and instead suggested casting in all cases to maintain uniformity.

Gave Acked-by
reviews.raw_body:
+1.  My main argument for casting in the 1-byte and 2-byte cases is consistency
above all else, using a mask for the 4-byte case defeats that goal.

2026-07-07.patch_summary: This patch series fixes bugs in the handling of emulated port I/O operations in the TDX guest #VE handler on x86 architecture. The first patch corrects an off-by-one error in the mask used for port I/O, while the second patch lifts a helper function from KVM to make it reusable by both KVM and the #VE handler. The third patch fixes 32-bit port IN operations by zero-extending them into RAX as per x86 semantics.
